title: China opens Pinglu Canal, air cargo drops, Shanghai omitted
metaDescription: Pinglu Canal cuts costs to South-east Asia, Hong Kong to Europe air cargo down 30%, and Gemini drops Shanghai from Asia shuttle. What to do this week.
bottomLine: China opens the Pinglu Canal on 15 September, halving transport costs from Nanning to South-east Asia. Hong Kong to Europe air cargo tonnages fell 30% year on year in August as EU duty changes persist. Gemini dropped Shanghai from its Asia shuttle, citing reliability, whilst typhoon delays at Shanghai and Ningbo exceed 10 days.

stories.headline: China opens Pinglu Canal on 15 September, halving costs to South-east Asia
stories.tldr: The $10.8bn Pinglu Canal opens 15 September, cutting transport costs from Nanning to Qinzhou port by half to around $190 per 40ft container.
stories.whatHappened:
China opens the Pinglu Canal on 15 September, a 134.2 km waterway connecting Nanning in Guangxi to Beibu Gulf. The canal accommodates vessels up to 5,000 tonnes. Trucking goods from Nanning to Qinzhou port currently costs around $387 per 40ft container. Feedering or barging along the canal could halve that cost.

China's Maritime Safety Administration released a nautical chart on 7 September covering the canal's seaward section, with 127 navigation marks installed. The opening coincides with the 23rd China-Asean Expo in Nanning, 17-21 September. South-east Asia is China's largest trading partner, with $766bn of trade in the first seven months of 2026.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you source from Guangxi or neighbouring provinces and ship to South-east Asia, this canal matters. The route cuts distance and cost, and you should ask your forwarder whether barging to Qinzhou beats trucking to Shenzhen or Guangzhou.

The canal targets vessels up to 5,000 tonnes, which means feeder and barge services rather than mainline ships. If you ship LCL or part-container volumes to Vietnam, Thailand or Malaysia, ask whether your forwarder plans to use the canal and what the transit time looks like.

The timing aligns with peak season. If your Q4 production is in Guangxi or Yunnan, barging to Qinzhou and transhipping to South-east Asia could shave days off your lead time. The canal is new infrastructure, so expect teething problems with scheduling and documentation in the first weeks.
stories.hotTake: Halving the cost from Nanning to the port is real money if you have volume there. The canal is not for everyone, but if you are sourcing in Guangxi and shipping to South-east Asia, your forwarder should have a quote ready by mid-September. If they do not, you are using the wrong forwarder.
actions: Ask your forwarder whether they plan to use the Pinglu Canal for South-east Asia shipments and request a rate comparison against trucking to Guangzhou or Shenzhen
If you source in Guangxi, Yunnan or western Guangdong, request a transit-time estimate for barge to Qinzhou plus feeder to your destination port
Expect documentation and scheduling delays in the first month; avoid using the canal for time-critical Q4 shipments until October

stories.headline: Hong Kong to Europe air cargo down 30% as EU duty changes persist
stories.tldr: Hong Kong to Europe air cargo tonnages fell 30% year on year in August, with spot rates dropping to $4.34 per kilo from $5.22 in June.
stories.whatHappened:
Hong Kong to Europe air cargo volumes fell 30% year on year in August and 24% below June levels. The drop follows the EU ending de minimis exemptions on imports under €150 on 1 July. Combined China and Hong Kong to Europe tonnages fell 14% year on year in both July and August.

Mainland China to Europe tonnages in August were down 5% year on year. Spot rates for China and Hong Kong to Europe fell from $5.22 per kilo in May and June to $4.34 per kilo in August. China and Hong Kong to US volumes in August were up 13% year on year, though growth slowed from 19% in May.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship ecommerce goods from Hong Kong to Europe by air, your volumes are part of that 30% drop. The EU duty changes are permanent, and your air freight model is now more expensive. You pay higher duties on arrival and your customers see longer clearance times.

Spot rates have fallen 17% since June, which is good news if you are still using air. The decline suggests carriers have overcapacity on the lane, so you have leverage to negotiate. Mainland China to Europe air cargo is holding better than Hong Kong, down only 5% year on year in August, so if you can shift your dispatch point north, you might find better rates and capacity.

The US lane is growing strongly, up 13% year on year in August, but the growth rate is slowing from 19% in May. If you split your air cargo between Europe and the US, you should see better pricing and space availability to the US.
stories.hotTake: The Hong Kong to Europe air lane is broken for low-value ecommerce and it is not coming back. Rates are down because demand is down, not because carriers are competing for your business. If you are still shipping small parcels by air from Hong Kong to Europe, you are paying for a service that no longer makes commercial sense.
actions: Renegotiate your Hong Kong to Europe air rates now, using the 17% spot rate decline as leverage
Shift dispatch to mainland China if possible, where air cargo to Europe is down only 5% and capacity is better
Review your ecommerce fulfilment model for Europe; bonded warehousing in the EU or rail freight may now beat air

stories.headline: Gemini drops Shanghai from Asia shuttle, citing reliability
stories.tldr: Gemini Cooperation is merging two Asia shuttle services and dropping Shanghai from the rotation, with the change taking effect 23 September.
stories.whatHappened:
Maersk announced it will merge its A04 and A14 intra-Asia shuttle services into a single enhanced A14 service, dropping a call at Shanghai. The final A04 sailing departs Dalian on 23 September. The existing A04 service runs Dalian-Tianjin-Busan-Shanghai, feeding northern Chinese and South Korean shipments to mainline services at Shanghai.

The revised A14 service starts 26 September with a rotation of Tianjin-Tanjung Pelepas-Singapore-Xiamen-Tianjin-Dalian-Busan. Calls at Busan drop from two per week to one. Typhoon Saudel caused terminal disruptions at Shanghai and Ningbo last week, resulting in vessel delays exceeding 10 days in the most severe cases.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you consolidate cargo in northern China and rely on Shanghai for transhipment to Europe or the US, you now have one fewer feeder option. The omission of Shanghai forces you to use Tanjung Pelepas or Singapore as your hub, which adds a leg and a potential delay.

The change signals that Gemini is prioritising reliability over port coverage, and Shanghai congestion is the likely reason. Vessel waiting times exceeding 10 days mean feeder schedules are breaking down. If your mainline service calls Shanghai, ask your carrier whether your feeder connection is still reliable.

Busan calls drop from two per week to one, which matters if you source in South Korea and consolidate there. You have half the weekly capacity you had before, and you need to book earlier to secure space.
stories.hotTake: Dropping Shanghai from a shuttle service is a big call, and it tells you congestion at the world's largest container port is worse than the carriers are saying in public. If your feeder schedule includes Shanghai, assume it is unreliable until you see three consecutive weeks of on-time arrivals.
actions: Check whether your northern China cargo currently moves on the A04 service and confirm your forwarder has rebooked you on the revised A14 or an alternative
If you consolidate in northern China for Europe or US destinations, ask your forwarder for a Tanjung Pelepas or Singapore routing and compare transit times
Plan for extended delays if your mainline service calls Shanghai or Ningbo; add 10 days to your lead time until congestion clears

stories.headline: Evergreen operates 58,000 IoT reefer containers with real-time monitoring
stories.tldr: Evergreen Marine now operates 58,000 reefer containers with IoT technology, transmitting real-time data on temperature, humidity and location.
stories.whatHappened:
Evergreen Marine operates around 58,000 reefer containers equipped with Internet of Things technology, the carrier announced at Asia Fruit Logistica 2026 in Hong Kong. The IoT-enabled containers transmit real-time information on location, temperature, humidity and operating status. The system issues alerts when it detects temperature deviations, unauthorised door openings or equipment problems.

Evergreen offers Controlled Atmosphere reefer services that regulate oxygen and carbon dioxide levels inside containers, slowing ripening for products including bananas, avocados and grapes. New reefer containers are adopting variable-speed compressors that adjust operation according to cooling requirements, designed to reduce energy consumption.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship fresh produce, dairy or pharmaceuticals from China, real-time reefer monitoring reduces the risk of spoilage claims. You can see temperature excursions as they happen and respond before the cargo is ruined. That matters for high-value, time-sensitive products where a single temperature failure can wipe out a shipment.

Controlled Atmosphere technology extends shelf life, which gives you more time between harvest and retail. If you ship fruit from China to Europe or North America, CA reefers let you use slower, cheaper ocean routes instead of air freight. The cost per container is higher, but the cost per tonne is lower if the product arrives in saleable condition.

The shift to preventive maintenance means fewer reefer breakdowns in transit. Evergreen is using data to predict failures and swap out equipment before it stops working.
stories.hotTake: IoT reefers are table stakes now, not a premium service. If your carrier cannot show you real-time temperature data for your shipment, you are using the wrong carrier. The cost of spoilage is too high to trust a reefer that phones home only when it breaks.
actions: Ask your carrier whether your next reefer shipment will be on an IoT-enabled container and request access to the monitoring dashboard
If you ship fresh produce with a shelf-life issue, request a quote for Controlled Atmosphere reefer service and compare the cost against air freight
Review your insurance coverage for reefer shipments; real-time monitoring gives you evidence for claims but does not replace insurance

faq.question: What is the Pinglu Canal and when does it open?
faq.answer: The Pinglu Canal is a 134.2 km waterway connecting Nanning in Guangxi to Beibu Gulf. It opens 15 September 2026. The canal accommodates vessels up to 5,000 tonnes and cuts transport costs from Nanning to Qinzhou port by around half, from $387 to roughly $190 per 40ft container. It targets cargo moving from south-west China to South-east Asia.

faq.question: Why did air cargo volumes from Hong Kong to Europe drop so much?
faq.answer: Hong Kong to Europe air cargo fell 30% year on year in August 2026 because the EU ended its de minimis exemption on imports under €150 on 1 July. Ecommerce sellers using air freight from Hong Kong now pay full duties and VAT on arrival. Spot rates fell from $5.22 per kilo in June to $4.34 in August, a 17% drop.

faq.question: Why did Maersk drop Shanghai from its Asia shuttle service?
faq.answer: Maersk merged its A04 and A14 shuttle services and dropped Shanghai from the rotation, effective 23 September 2026. The carrier said the change was intended to enhance schedule reliability. Congestion at Shanghai and Ningbo has worsened, with typhoon delays exceeding 10 days. The revised service calls Tianjin, Tanjung Pelepas, Singapore, Xiamen, Dalian and Busan.

faq.question: What are IoT-enabled reefer containers and why do they matter?
faq.answer: IoT-enabled reefer containers transmit real-time data on temperature, humidity, location and equipment status. Evergreen operates 58,000 of these containers. The system issues alerts when it detects temperature deviations or equipment problems, allowing response before cargo spoils. This reduces loss risk for perishable goods like fresh produce, dairy and pharmaceuticals.

faq.question: Should I use the Pinglu Canal for my Q4 shipments to South-east Asia?
faq.answer: The Pinglu Canal opens 15 September, mid-peak season. The cost saving is real, cutting transport from Nanning to Qinzhou by roughly half. However, expect teething problems with scheduling and documentation in the first weeks. If your Q4 shipments are time-critical, avoid the canal until October. If you have non-urgent cargo, the canal is worth using for the cost saving.
